cards.front: What does PXE stand for and what does it do?
cards.back: Preboot eXecution Environment. The BIOS pulls an OS installer from a PXE server across the network, with no local media required.

cards.front: What is an ISO image?
cards.back: An exact disk image of an optical disc, stored as a single file. Can be mounted as if it were a physical disk.

cards.front: What is a clean install?
cards.back: Wipes the partition and reinstalls the OS from scratch. No previous files, apps, or settings remain.

cards.front: What is an in-place upgrade?
cards.back: Installs a newer OS while keeping existing applications, user data, and settings.

cards.front: What is a zero-touch deployment?
cards.back: Fully automated OS install + configuration. User opens a new device, turns it on, waits for everything (domain join, email, apps) to configure itself.

cards.front: What is image deployment?
cards.back: Build one reference image (OS + apps + configuration), then push it to many machines.

cards.front: What does a repair installation do?
cards.back: Overwrites operating system files but leaves user data and configuration in place. Windows-specific fix for a broken OS.

cards.front: When would you load third-party drivers during installation?
cards.back: When the installer's stock drivers do not recognize your storage controller or network interface. There is usually a prompt during install.

cards.front: GPT partition style: maximum partitions per drive?
GPT partition style requires what kind of BIOS?
cards.back: UEFI BIOS.

cards.front: MBR maximum partition size?
cards.back: 2 TB.

cards.front: MBR maximum number of primary partitions?
cards.back: 4 primary partitions. (Use 1 extended partition with logical partitions if more are needed.)

cards.front: On an MBR disk, are logical partitions inside an extended partition bootable?
cards.back: No. Only primary partitions are bootable on MBR.

cards.front: In Microsoft terminology, what is a 'volume'?
cards.back: A formatted partition.

cards.front: Quick format vs full format: which actually erases the data?
cards.back: Full format writes zeros across the entire disk and actually erases the data. Quick format only rewrites the file system table; old data is still technically recoverable.

cards.front: Which format type is the default in Windows 10 / 11 installation?
cards.back: Quick format.

cards.front: Which Windows tool checks if a system meets Windows 11 requirements?
cards.back: PC Health Check.

cards.front: What three hardware features does Windows 11 specifically require?
cards.back: TPM 2.0, UEFI BIOS, and Secure Boot enabled. (Plus a supported 64-bit CPU.)

cards.front: Which Windows utility shows the TPM details for the local system?
cards.back: tpm.msc

cards.front: Where in Windows do you check the Secure Boot State?
cards.back: System Information utility, System Summary section, 'Secure Boot State' line.

cards.front: What is the difference between a feature update and a quality update?
cards.back: Quality updates are monthly bug/security fixes. Feature updates add new capabilities, typically every 6-12 months.

cards.front: What is the recovery partition?
cards.back: A hidden local partition holding OS installer files, used for repair or re-install when the running OS fails.

cards.front: What happens if you enable BIOS compatibility mode to boot a GPT disk on a legacy BIOS?
cards.back: Secure Boot is disabled. Many newer OSes will not run without Secure Boot.
